page0.text:
"Guess I'll work up a quick sweat if I have so much time."
Morning exercise is my daily routine, so I might as well do some light workouts.
page0.sourceUnit: セイバールート二日目-05:page0:1

page1.text:
There's a respectable dojo built in the Emiya house.
It was added as sort of an afterthought when the house was constructed.
Which is why this dojo wasn't built for a specific purpose.
page1.sourceUnit: セイバールート二日目-05:page1:1

page2.text:
"Well, Fuji-nee uses it on a whim sometimes."
Fuji-nee apparently used this place as her playground even before I came to this house.
But then I became Kiritsugu's disciple and started using this place more often. Fuji-nee hated me for that for a while.
page2.sourceUnit: セイバールート二日目-05:page2:1

page3.text:
"Anyway."
There's only one thing I do here.
Training to be a mage means I can't neglect training my body.
One of the conditions of being a mage is maintaining yourself at your physical peak.
page3.sourceUnit: セイバールート二日目-05:page3:1

page4.text:
When Kiritsugu was still alive, he and I sparred often.
Well, more that he just kicked my ass every time, so I never really learned how to win myself.
But at least I learned the difference between a fight and a battle.
In other words, I learned the difference between killing and beating an opponent, and how to conduct myself in each situation.
page4.sourceUnit: セイバールート二日目-05:page4:1

page5.text:
Knowledge and experience are different.
Without the knowledge to know the difference, it's hard to tell if you've gotten yourself into a fight or a massacre.
page5.sourceUnit: セイバールート二日目-05:page5:1

page6.text:
It's as simple as that.
Learning magecraft means that there is a risk of perishing on your own, as well as the risk of having to fight.
And to mages, that means killing each other.
That's why Kiritsugu wanted to teach me that I must always be ready to face death.
page6.sourceUnit: セイバールート二日目-05:page6:1

page7.text:
But the person reminding me of that lesson is long gone.
So the only thing I can do alone is some simple exercises.
Stretching, push-ups, sit-ups...it's no different than what the members of the kyudou club do in the morning.
The only difference is in the intensity.
page7.sourceUnit: セイバールート二日目-05:page7:1
